method: Heuristic market-prioritization scores from reviewed official municipal sources. Scores measure research friction, not legal risk or permit eligibility.

municipalities.name: Chicago
evidence_basis: Single-event and 180-day special-event paths are distinct.
Multi-event applications move through BACP to CDPH Food Protection Services.
A commissary, restaurant or shared kitchen must have an inspection within six months of application.
Mobile Food Preparers must already hold a Chicago license and sanitation certificate before applying for a special event.

requirements.label: Choose the applicable single-event or 180-day special-event path
Provide applicable sanitation certificate and existing City mobile-food license for Mobile Food Preparers
Confirm commissary, restaurant or shared-kitchen inspection recency

municipalities.name: Evanston
evidence_basis: Mobile Food Vehicle licenses are annual and non-transferable.
Temporary and seasonal event food permits have separate terms and fees.
Event submissions are requested at least ten business days before the event; late and near-event submissions face penalties or non-approval risk.
Food trucks at temporary events must provide their current Food Establishment License and outside-Evanston kitchens must provide a recent local health inspection report.
Mobile vending has time and location restrictions, including school-distance restrictions.

requirements.label: Hold the applicable Evanston mobile food vendor license
Obtain event-organizer approval before applying for a temporary or seasonal food permit
Provide current food-establishment license and outside-jurisdiction inspection report when applicable

municipalities.name: Skokie
evidence_basis: Public-event mobile food trucks require an Environmental Health license.
Multiple-event and single-event license paths are distinct.
Multiple-event licenses renew annually on a May 1-April 30 cycle and fees vary by service type.

requirements.label: Select single-event or multiple-event mobile-food-truck licensure
Renew a multiple-event license for each May-April licensing period

municipalities.name: Elgin
evidence_basis: For the 2026 season, applicable food trucks, trailers, grills and deep fryers require a pre-event fire inspection.
Day-of fire inspection carries a stated $100 fee while scheduled pre-inspection can be free.
Temporary and seasonal food-handling paths differ, and private-property events can add a temporary-use permit dependency.
Temporary food handling applications for special events are due no later than seven days before the event.
Food may not be sold in Elgin parks or streets or from moving vehicles under the cited seasonal/temporary food-handling page.

requirements.label: Complete annual fire inspection when operating an applicable truck, trailer, grill or deep fryer
Obtain host or property-owner pre-approval before temporary-food application when applicable
Add a temporary-use permit for qualifying private-property events

municipalities.name: Oak Park
evidence_basis: A Temporary Food License is required before serving food or beverages at a public event, subject to stated exceptions.
The official Environmental Health page routes applicants to a Temporary Food License Application and Commissary Agreement Form.
Oak Park inspects temporary food establishments and regulates food-safety compliance.

requirements.label: Obtain a Temporary Food License before qualifying public-event food service
Confirm whether a commissary agreement applies to the vendor's preparation model

municipalities.name: Naperville
evidence_basis: Food vendors must be permitted.
Food trucks are prohibited from vending on public streets in Naperville.
Applications are managed through the City's Civic Access portal.

requirements.label: Plan operations around the prohibition on food-truck vending on public streets

municipalities.name: Cicero
municipalities.evidence_scope: Base Town business-license workflow only; food-specific requirements require a separate Health Department review before client delivery.
evidence_basis: All businesses must obtain a Town business license before operating.
The cited workflow starts with an in-person Business License Department application and a non-refundable application fee.
Zoning approval is required, followed by inspections involving Fire, Building, Electrical and Health departments.
Additional business and insurance/tax documentation follows the department-approval sequence.

requirements.label: Complete the Town business-license application before operating
Obtain zoning approval for the intended business use
Schedule Fire, Building, Electrical and Health property inspections in the Town workflow
Confirm food-vendor-specific Health Department requirements before relying on this base-license map
